figures.finding: In Guinea-Bissau, as in every OHADA state, a minor may hold shares in a company where liability stops at the contribution (a SARL, an SA or SAS, or as a limited partner) but cannot be a partner liable for the company's debts beyond it, and cannot trade unless emancipated; the Uniform Act sets no age of its own for a SARL's manager, who must be a natural person, so a manager's capacity is the national civil law's (majority or emancipation).

figures.applies: Guinea-Bissau is a state party to the OHADA Treaty (ratified 15 January 1994, in force 20 February 1996, per the treaty's ratification table), whose Uniform Acts are directly applicable there, notwithstanding domestic law (art. 10). A minor's shares are subscribed through the legal administrator.

sources.said: Les mineurs et les majeurs incapables ne peuvent être associés d’une société dans laquelle ils seraient tenus des dettes sociales au‐delà de leurs apports.
La société à responsabilité limitée est gérée par une ou plusieurs personnes physiques, associées ou non.
Le mineur, sauf s'il est émancipé, ne peut avoir la qualité de commerçant ni effectuer des actes de commerce.
Les actes uniformes sont directement applicables et obligatoires dans les Etats-Parties, nonobstant toute disposition contraire de droit interne, antérieure ou postérieure.

figures.finding: The minimum age for employment in Guinea-Bissau is sixteen under the Labour Code promulgated in July 2022, which raised it from fourteen; no light-work age below it is set.

value.lightNote: the earlier law allowed work from 14; the 2022 code's light-work rule is not reported
value.law: Código do Trabalho (promulgated July 2022), arts. 1, 3, 288, 347, 350, 520 (minimum age), 354-355 (hazardous work)
